items.text: Are you one of those people that sees faces in inanimate objects?

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: one of those people that sees faces in inanimate objects

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: that sees faces in inanimate objects

items.text: Researchers at the National Institutes of Health have been trying to find out why this is.

level1.label: 谓语
level1.text: have been trying to find out

items.text: They have pinpointed a circuit in an evolutionarily ancient part of the brain.
It's called the superior colliculus, and it helps us recognise facial features.
It triggers movement of the eyes, turning of the head and enables us to detect faces.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: movement of the eyes, turning of the head

items.text: This study helps us understand face pareidolia - the common psychological phenomenon where the brain perceives illusions of faces in objects, like seeing faces in the clouds, exteriors of houses or even in a slice of toast.

level1.label: 同位语
level1.text: the common psychological phenomenon where the brain perceives illusions of faces in objects

level2.label: 定语从句
level2.text: where the brain perceives illusions of faces in objects

items.text: A study carried out by Susan Wardle showed that the parts of the human brain that respond to faces are sensitive to the shapes of other objects, and that our visual system is optimised for detecting face-like structures.

level1.label: 主语
level1.text: A study carried out by Susan Wardle

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that the parts of the human brain that respond to faces are sensitive to the shapes of other objects

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: that our visual system is optimised for detecting face-like structures

items.text: To test whether the superior colliculus might help in face detection specifically, researchers assembled a collection of images, including faces, biological non-face objects, like hands and arms, and other miscellaneous items.

level1.label: 状语
level1.text: To test whether the superior colliculus might help in face detection specifically

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: a collection of images, including faces, biological non-face objects, like hands and arms, and other miscellaneous items

level2.label: 宾语从句
level2.text: whether the superior colliculus might help in face detection specifically

level2.label: 后置定语
level2.text: including faces, biological non-face objects, like hands and arms, and other miscellaneous items

items.text: They then showed these images to adult monkeys in their peripheral field and recorded neural responses in the superior colliculus.
It was found that detection of faces was much faster and preferred by neurons.

level1.label: 主语从句
level1.text: that detection of faces was much faster and preferred by neurons

items.text: This explains how our brains do it.
But why do our brains do it?
According to Dr Amanda Robinson at the University of Queensland, face pareidolia tells us a lot about how we recognise social cues.
We can determine whether the person or thing looking at us is a threat because of their facial expression.

level1.label: 宾语从句
level1.text: whether the person or thing looking at us is a threat

items.text: Richard Krauzlis, senior author of the study, explained that "quick recognition is a key skill in humans and other primates", such as gorillas and chimps.

level1.label: 表语
level1.text: a key skill in humans and other primates

items.text: Additionally, biologists have observed human facial recognition and neural developments among species ranging from dogs, sheep, birds and even some insects.

level1.label: 宾语
level1.text: human facial recognition and neural developments

items.text: What we know about recognition of faces and expression can further inform research on conditions such as autism, where face detection and recognition are often impaired from early childhood.

level1.label: 主语从句
level1.text: What we know about recognition of faces and expression

items.text: It also helps us understand why we think we saw a friendly face in the living room wallpaper.

level1.label: 宾语补足语
level1.text: understand why we think we saw a friendly face in the living room wallpaper

level2.label: 宾语从句
level2.text: why we think we saw a friendly face in the living room wallpaper
